bugs: Rejects UTF-8 BOM-prefixed CSVs (the default Excel 'CSV UTF-8' export) at upload with 422 'must have a header row', because the header is only trimmed with trim() and the BOM is never stripped (StoreImportRequest.php:28, ProcessImport.php:80). Confirmed by a probe.
Header matching is case-sensitive, so 'SKU,Name,Price,Stock' is rejected with 422 (probe confirmed).
With Tries(3) plus a counter reset, a retry after a mid-file crash counts products created on the earlier attempt as 'updated', so the created/updated split is wrong (ProcessImport.php:38-46, 116).
The file handle opened in the FormRequest after() hook is never closed (StoreImportRequest.php:26).
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:31 – Gate::authorize inside the controller where route ->can('view','import') would do the job; the show() action also has an unused Request $request parameter (line 29).
app/Http/Requests/StoreImportRequest.php:28 – the HTTP FormRequest depends on the job's COLUMNS constant, which couples validation to the job class.
app/Http/Requests/StoreImportRequest.php:26 – fgetcsv(fopen(...)) inline, with the handle leaked.
app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:26 – $import->refresh() makes an extra query only to pick up DB defaults (model $attributes would avoid it).
tests/Feature/ProductImportTest.php:252-257 – a manual try/catch plus $this->fail to simulate a queue failure.
strengths: Clean, modern Laravel 13 job: #[Tries, Backoff, Timeout, DeleteWhenMissingModels] attributes, Storage::readStream with ?? throw, and try/finally fclose.
Retries are safe to run twice: row errors are deleted and counts reset on retry, and a completed import is skipped.
updateOrCreate together with wasRecentlyCreated is the most idiomatic upsert-with-count.
Header is validated at upload in the FormRequest after() hook, so a bad file fails fast.
Fixes the guest-redirect behaviour for API routes in bootstrap (redirectGuestsTo), so non-JSON guest requests get 401 instead of 500.
Very thorough tests: retry/idempotency, interrupted retry, failed hook, 5MB boundary, reordered and quoted columns, end-to-end run.

bugs: A guest making a non-JSON request (e.g. GET /api/imports/1 without Accept: application/json) gets a 500 because the auth middleware redirects to the undefined 'login' route. bootstrap was not adjusted (probe confirmed). JSON clients correctly get 401.
With Tries(1) and no retry, any transient DB or storage error permanently marks the import failed. This is acceptable, but there is no recovery path.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:48 – the queued job depends on StoreImportRequest::COLUMNS (domain code reaching into the HTTP layer); the constant belongs on the model, an enum, or the job.
app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:83-86 and app/Http/Requests/StoreImportRequest.php:51-54 – the header-normalising closure (BOM/trim/lowercase) is duplicated verbatim.
app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:133 – upsert() mutates counts through an array &$counts reference parameter; returning the outcome would be cleaner.
app/Models/Import.php:19-25 – $attributes duplicates the migration defaults, and uses the raw 'queued' string instead of ImportStatus::Queued->value.
app/Models/Import.php:43 – ordering is baked into the rowErrors relation definition.
strengths: Authorization is declared on the route with ->can('view','import'), which keeps the controller actions to one line each.
Handles real-world CSVs: strips a UTF-8 BOM, lowercases headers, allows extra and reordered columns, and parses RFC-4180 with escape: '' (which also avoids the PHP 8.4 escape-default issue).
ProcessImport::dispatch()->afterCommit(), the #[WithoutRelations] constructor attribute and #[Tries]/#[Timeout] attributes are modern queue idioms.
Unreadable files and bad headers in the job go through $this->fail(), which sends them to the failed() hook that sets the Failed status, and the status guard prevents reprocessing.
Errors are bulk-inserted in batches, products are saved from $validator->safe()->only(), and rows that are blank or whitespace-only are skipped.
Tests mostly exercise the full HTTP flow, with exact JSON assertions on reasons and row numbers, plus BOM/case/extra-column, row ordering and unreadable-file failure paths.

v.rationale: I rank impl-2 first and impl-1 second. Both test suites pass (impl-1: 23 tests, impl-2: 22 tests). The two implementations are structurally very close: enum status, FormRequest with a header check in after(), a policy, a JsonResource, a queued job with Laravel 13 attributes, a queued markdown mailable, and batched row errors. My edge-case probes found the bugs that separate them. impl-1 rejects UTF-8 BOM-prefixed CSVs (the default Excel UTF-8 export) and uppercase headers with a 422. That is a common real-world failure for a product import. impl-1 also leaks a file handle in the FormRequest, and its retry reset miscounts created rows as 'updated' after a partial crash. impl-2 handles BOM, case and extra columns, and parses RFC-4180 correctly. It authorizes on the route with ->can(), dispatches with afterCommit, and uses #[WithoutRelations]. Its main flaws are a 500 for a guest making a non-JSON request (impl-1 fixed this in bootstrap), the job depending on a constant on the FormRequest, and a duplicated header-normalising closure. impl-1 has slightly stronger retry/idempotency design and tests, but impl-2's input handling is more correct and its controller and routes are more idiomatic.
